text: Nepal PM to reach Delhi on Sunday for first foreign bilateral trip - what's on agenda. NEW DELHI: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will begin a two-day state visit to India on Sunday, his first overseas bilateral state visit since taking office in March."The visit will serve as an important opportunity to review our wide-ranging cooperative partnership with a forward-looking perspective, maximising mutual benefits for the peoples of both countries," Nepal's foreign ministry said in a statement.Shah, an ex-Kathmandu mayor and a former rapper, will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation comprising finance minister Swarnim Wagle, foreign affairs minister Shishir Khanal, his chief advisor Kumar Byanjankar, and other senior government officials. Balendra Shah's itinerary in New Delhi Shah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday, after which they will jointly inaugurate several energy-related projects. The two sides will also sign and exchange bilateral agreements covering various areas of cooperation.The two prime ministers will address a joint press conference, followed by a luncheon hosted by PM Modi in honour of the visiting Nepali leader.During his visit, Shah will also call on President Droupadi Murmu and pay tributes at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat.He is also scheduled to attend the Nepal-India Business Forum, which aims to strengthen trade and economic ties between the two countries. What's likely to be discussed According to ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, India and Nepal are expected to discuss issues including development cooperation and people-to-people ties."All these issues will be discussed: development cooperation, people-to-people ties, energy ties, connectivity, and some of the newer areas of cooperation such as startups, technology, innovation, and sports. Cricket links have also become an important connection between India and Nepal. This is a very important visit for us," Jaiswal told reporters at a weekly news briefing in New Delhi on Friday.Shah is also expected to discuss Indian assistance for the reconstruction of areas affected by the devastating floods in August, Reuters reported, citing Nepalese officials.The August 26 floods killed 1,500 people, left more than 5,200 missing and destroyed roads, bridges, power plants, farms and homes.Nepal is also likely to discuss with India an additional route for commercial flights from the west to Bhairahawa, near Lumbini, the birthplace of Gautam Buddha, and the tourist city of Pokhara. Karan Manral is a journalist at the Times of India. He covers politics, social issues, and international affairs, exploring stories that affect people’s everyday lives. He also writes explainers to make these stories easier for readers to follow.
